body.statement: For every well-typed explicit instance \(I\), \(\mathsf{SC\mbox{-}CTFID}(I)\) terminates and never returns \(O\). It returns a circuit \(C\) if and only if the following uniform identification condition holds: for every \(p\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{feas}}\) with \(\mathcal F_+(p)\ne\varnothing\), and all \(\theta,\theta'\in\mathcal F_+(p)\), \(H(\theta)K(\theta')=H(\theta')K(\theta)\). On that branch, \(C(p)=H(\theta)/K(\theta)\) for every such \(p,\theta\). For an exact numerical \(p\notin\mathcal P_{\mathrm{feas}}\), \(\operatorname{Eval}\) returns \(\mathsf{infeasible}\); for \(p\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{feas}}\) with \(\mathcal F_+(p)=\varnothing\), it returns \(\mathsf{undefined\mbox{-}zero\mbox{-}denominator}\). If uniform identification fails, the algorithm returns a verifier-accepted \((\Gamma,\mathcal M^-,\mathcal M^+)\) with both models in \(\mathfrak M_{sc}(G,\operatorname{inc},\mathcal X)\), the declared alphabets, source incidence, legality, and identical complete laws for every \(r\in\mathcal R\), but positive denominators and unequal values of \(q\).
body.justification: The formula-or-verifiable-same-class-countermodel dichotomy is the completeness contract absent from cyclic Layer-3 identification.
body.gap: CorreaLeeBareinboim2021, Algorithms 1--2 and Theorems 5--6, proves this contract for recursive acyclic SCMs; ForreMooij2020, Theorem 9.10 and Remark 9.11, gives sound cyclic interventional identification without completeness.
body.consumer: The cfid package gains feedback-capable symbolic output or a replayable failure certificate with exact domain statuses.
